definition: Angel_F is a fictional child artificial intelligence that has been used in art performances worldwide focused on the issues of digital liberties, intellectual property and on the evolution of language and behaviour in information society.
details: The character was created by Salvatore Iaconesi in 2007 as a hack to the Biodoll art performance by Italian artist Franca Formenti. The project was later joined by Oriana Persico who curated communication and part of the theoretical approaches of the action. The Angel_F project has been featured in books, magazines, national televisions, and has been invited to many conferences and events, both academic and artistic.

explainer.lead: Angel_F was a fictional child artificial intelligence at the centre of an art project about how networked technology shapes language, identity and behaviour. Created by Salvatore Iaconesi in 2007 and later developed with Oriana Persico, it generated text from contributed material and web activity, then appeared in online dialogues, conferences and public performances. Its child-like story made questions about digital liberties and intellectual property tangible to audiences.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a make-believe baby that learns to talk from words people give it and from places they visit online. Angel_F was presented as that baby: it began inside its digital mother's website, wrote strange messages on blogs, and attended real events on a laptop carried in a baby stroller. It was not a real child, but an artwork designed to get people thinking about freedom, identity and ownership on the internet.
tiers.practitioner: Treat Angel_F as a sociotechnical performance rather than a reproducible software product: its Talker component built a linguistic network from user-supplied text and web clips, while browser-based spyware, crawling techniques and a content database supported its online behaviour. Generated sentences were published through its interface and selected blogs, with Talker Mind adding academic texts through a multi-blog structure and Presence providing peer-to-peer chat and file sharing. The main interpretive pitfall is mistaking its staged learning narrative and generated dialogue for demonstrated general intelligence; its observation of browsing activity also makes privacy part of the work, not a neutral implementation detail.
tiers.paperLevel: Angel_F, a backronym for Autonomous Non Generative E-volitive Life_Form, can be described as: narrative digital identity + Talker linguistic AI + web observation and crawling + human-authored corpora + online and physical performance interfaces. It originated in 2007 when Iaconesi used Talker to animate the digital child of Franca Formenti's Biodoll, conceived with Derrick de Kerckhove, and concluded in 2009 with the book 'Angel F. Diario di una intelligenza artificiale'. Its behaviour depended on contributed texts, collected web content and narrative staging, so the project does not establish autonomous human-like learning or cognition.

explainer.example: At the Talker Mind virtual school, Massimo Canevacci, Antonio Caronia, Carlo Formenti, Derrick de Kerckhove and Luigi Pagliarini fed their texts and academic articles to Angel_F. A multi-blog structure presented these contributions as asynchronous lessons, continuing the fiction that the AI was developing like a child at school.

usedIn.name: Art performances
usedIn.detail: Angel_F appeared worldwide through generated text, interactive graphics and a laptop mounted on a baby stroller.

usedIn.name: Academic conferences
usedIn.detail: Its first academic presentation was at the 2007 Glocal & Outsiders conference in Prague, alongside the Biodoll.

usedIn.name: Digital-rights activism
usedIn.detail: It contributed to Internet Governance Forum discussions and the 2008 Freedom not Fear event on privacy and civil liberties.

usedIn.name: Talker Mind
usedIn.detail: Five professors supplied texts and articles for simulated asynchronous lessons delivered through multiple blogs.

explainer.intuition: The project used the familiar story of a child growing up to frame an AI as something formed by the people, texts and systems around it. That story let audiences encounter network culture as a relationship with a digital being rather than only as an abstract technical debate.
howItWorks: The Biodoll website supplied the narrative setting, with Angel_F growing like a virus through its databases and interfaces.
Browser-based spyware inferred major portals visited by site users, while crawling techniques supported navigation of websites and portals.
People fed text and web clips to the Talker linguistic AI, building the language material available to Angel_F.
Angel_F generated sentences from its stored content and published them through its interface and selected blogs.
Talker Mind, the Presence peer-to-peer system and a stroller-mounted laptop extended the performance into lessons, messaging and physical events.
explainer.whyItMatters: Angel_F connected language generation and online observation with public debates about privacy, intellectual property, digital freedoms and fluid identities. Its appearances in artistic, academic and activist settings turned those issues into encounters people could directly watch and discuss.
misconceptions: Angel_F was a fictional digital child in an art project, not evidence of a conscious or human-like AI.
Its language came from contributed material and software processes, not from an isolated mind inventing everything itself.
The baby-stroller laptop was a physical performance interface, not a robot body with independent movement.
